samples.summary: BoardToolbar adopting the focus-release hook defeats the board's documented "Space on a focused BoardToolbar toggle activates the button, not pan mode" guard for the mouse path
samples.evidence: `isEditableTarget` (packages/frontend/src/app/board/is-editable-target.ts:22-28) exists specifically so that `board-view.tsx:625`'s Space-for-pan handler bails when a BoardToolbar `<button>`/toggle has focus — see the comment at is-editable-target.ts:9 and the regression test at packages/frontend/src/app/board/is-editable-target.test.ts:50-55 ("a focused BoardToolbar toggle ... Space still activates the button"). With `useCanvasFocusRelease()` now mounted by BoardToolbar (board-toolbar.tsx:137) and the root marked `data-canvas-toolbar` (board-toolbar.tsx:186), every pointer-driven toolbar click blurs the control to `document.body` one task later, so `e.target` at the next keydown is the body and the guard never engages. Pressing Space right after clicking e.g. Select / Sticky note now enters pan mode instead of re-activating the button. Only Tab-driven focus (which the hook deliberately exempts) still reaches the guarded path. If the new behaviour is intended, the comment at is-editable-target.ts:9 and the test's rationale should be updated to say the button branch only covers keyboard-focused controls.

samples.summary: The keepalive exemption is scoped by attribute, not by whether a text-edit session is live, so keepalive-marked controls in a canvas toolbar never release focus even outside text edit
samples.evidence: `isReleasable` now bails for anything under `[data-text-edit-keepalive]` (packages/frontend/src/components/toolbar-focus-release.ts:76). Those attributes live on shared components (packages/frontend/src/components/text-formatting/text-format-group.tsx:245,290; font-size-picker.tsx:145; text-paragraph-group.tsx:82) that are reused verbatim by the board toolbar via TextEditSection (packages/frontend/src/app/slides/toolbar/text-edit-section.tsx:65-89). Any future/other placement of these components inside a `data-canvas-toolbar` root outside a live text-edit session silently reinstates issue #882 for those controls, since the hook cannot tell a live text box from a stale attribute. I could not find such a placement today (theme-builder-panel.tsx:172 is outside the toolbar root), hence low confidence; a state-based check (`editor.isTextEditing()`) rather than an attribute check would remove the hazard.

finding.summary: New global focus-release contradicts the existing "dismiss must restore focus to the trigger" contract of the keepalive dropdowns used by the slides text-edit toolbar, stranding focus on <body> while the in-place text box is still mounted
finding.evidence: `font-family-picker.tsx:155-158` — `if (family === null) { // No pick — let Radix restore focus to the trigger so Esc / outside-click dismiss does not strand focus on <body>. return; }` and the identical guard in `text-paragraph-group.tsx:94-101`. Both controls are rendered inside the slides text-edit toolbar (`packages/frontend/src/app/slides/toolbar/text-edit-section.tsx:65,89`), which now sits under `data-canvas-toolbar`. The new hook only clears its `pointerDriven` flag on `Tab`, so after the user opens one of these menus with the mouse and dismisses it with Escape or an outside click, Radix restores focus to the trigger, `focusin` fires inside the toolbar, and the deferred `releaseFocusToBody()` blurs the trigger. Because these triggers carry `data-text-edit-keepalive`, the docs text-box editor deliberately skipped its commit (`packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:736-751`) and the in-place editor is still mounted — but nothing holds focus any more. Subsequent keys now target `document.body`, which is exactly what `isEditableTarget()` gates on (`packages/slides/src/view/editor/interactions/keyboard.ts:177,211`), so Delete/Backspace deletes the element being edited and printable keys drive canvas rules instead of typing. Fix belongs in the new hook (skip release while the editor is in text-edit mode / for `[data-text-edit-keepalive]` controls).

verdict.reason: The claimed bypass is already guarded by the hook itself. `isReleasable()` in packages/frontend/src/components/toolbar-focus-release.ts:71-79 returns false for any element matching `[data-text-edit-keepalive]` (line 76, selector defined at line 43), and the deferred release at lines 120-122 only calls `releaseFocusToBody()` when `isReleasable(document.activeElement)` is true. Both controls the finding cites render that attribute on the actual DOM trigger: font-family-picker.tsx:133 (raw <button data-text-edit-keepalive>) and text-paragraph-group.tsx:82 via ToolbarButton, which spreads ...props onto <button> (packages/frontend/src/components/ui/toolbar.tsx:89-97). So when Radix restores focus to the trigger after Esc / outside-click dismiss, `document.activeElement` is a keepalive control and the release no-ops — focus is not stranded on <body>, and the docs text-box editor keepalive contract is preserved. A regression test asserts exactly this behaviour: toolbar-focus-release.test.tsx:85-93 clicks a `data-text-edit-keepalive` button, flushes the setTimeout(0), and expects activeElement to still be that button. The remedy the finding prescribes ("skip release for [data-text-edit-keepalive] controls") is already the implemented behaviour.

finding.summary: BoardToolbar reuses the same SlidesEditor keyboard gate but was not opted into the fix, so issue #882 remains reproducible on boards
finding.evidence: `packages/frontend/src/app/board/board-toolbar.tsx:178` renders `<Toolbar>` with no `data-canvas-toolbar` and never calls `useCanvasFocusRelease()`, while its own header comment (lines 91-106) states it drives the reused `SlidesEditor` and reuses the slides toolbar's leaf controls off the same `getToolbarState`. Since the shortcut gate lives in `packages/slides/src/view/editor/interactions/keyboard.ts` (shared by boards), every board toolbar button still parks focus on a `<button>` and silently kills arrow/Delete/z-order shortcuts.

verdict.reason: The finding claims BoardToolbar was never opted into the #882 focus-release fix. The file shows the opposite. `board-toolbar.tsx:5` imports `useCanvasFocusRelease`, `board-toolbar.tsx:137` calls it (preceded by a comment at lines 132-136 explicitly reasoning about the shared SlidesEditor shortcut gate and issue #882), and `board-toolbar.tsx:186` renders `<Toolbar data-canvas-toolbar="">` — the CANVAS_TOOLBAR_ATTR opt-in defined at toolbar-focus-release.ts:30. The reviewer's cited line 178 does not contain the `<Toolbar>` render at all (it is the `gridLabel` comment); the render is at 186 and carries the attribute. The mechanism genuinely connects: `useCanvasFocusRelease` (toolbar-focus-release.ts:89-134) installs document-level listeners and `isReleasable` (lines 71-79) matches BUTTON/role=button elements inside `[data-canvas-toolbar]`, releasing focus to body — exactly the remediation said to be missing. `BoardToolbar` is defined once (line 109) and rendered once (board-view.tsx:792), so there is no second unpatched board toolbar; remaining `<BoardToolbar` matches are archived design docs. Boards are wired identically to slides (slides/toolbar/index.tsx:70,110).
